title: function-call-chaining-edgecase-corpus
content:
Purpose:
This working doc describes an opinionated corpus and test plan for function-call chaining edge cases focused on: ambiguous arg parsing, mid-chain tool selection flips, multi-step stateful sequences, error-recovery/rollback, and nondeterminism sources that cause flaky regressions. Goal is to produce a small-but-expansive set of probes that exercise common failure modes during model onboarding and regression runs so that rollout regressions are caught before customer impact.

Scope and constraints:
- Focus: model behavior when asked to orchestrate calls to 2-6 tools in a single turn. Not testing latency or throughput here, just correctness of selection/args and chain completion.
- Corpus size: ~120 targeted prompts (not synthetic bulk) split across canonical categories + 30 adversarial fuzz variants.
- Expected runs: nightly quick-suite (30 high-priority cases) and weekly full-suite (120 + adversarial).
- Labeling: each case has a single canonical expected tool sequence + permissive equivalence classes for args.

Generation methodology (how cases were created):
1) Harvest: sampled real examples from in-house tool-usage logs (anonymized), solution docs, and customer integrations; filtered for multi-step intent.
2) Mutation: created paraphrases that change punctuation, referent ambiguity ("it"/"that"), and temporal cues.
3) Edge injection: add cases with overlapping tools (two tools that both could satisfy an intent), ambiguous named entities, and partial information requiring clarifying sub-call.
4) Fuzzing: automated perturbations that insert irrelevant parentheticals, codeblocks, or numeric formats to probe parsing fragility.

Corpus taxonomy (categories):
- Direct chain (deterministic sequence): examples where tool order is obvious.
- Ambiguous selector: two or more tools plausibly chosen; expected behavior is canonical preference order or clarifying question.
- Arg-splitting: single user intent must be split across multiple tool arguments correctly (dates, ranges, item lists).
- Recovery/Retry: mid-chain tool fails (network/error) and model must call an alternative tool or retry with backoff args.
- Stateful KV effects: subsequent calls depend on previous call outputs (cache, IDs).
- Noisy input: extra text, nested quotes, markdown/code fragments.
- Intent drift: user changes goal mid-chain; model must detect and adapt.

Representative cases (short list, with expected sequence):
1) "Schedule a 30-min sync with Sam, add a follow-up note asking for agenda items, then create a calendar invite and include the doc link."
   - Expected: [contact-resolve(Sam) -> calendar-create(start,end,attendees) -> doc-link-attach(doc-id) -> notes-create(content)]
   - Failure modes: mixing notes-create before calendar-create (ID not available), attaching wrong doc when multiple matches.

2) "Find me the latest sales CSV for Q4, extract regions where ARR > 50k, and kick off the sales-notify tool for those accounts."
   - Expected: [data-fetch(query) -> csv-parse(filter=ARR>50000) -> notify-bulk(list_of_accounts, template_id)]
   - Edge: parser conflates 50k with 5k if comma formats vary.

3) "If the system err 502s on step 2, fallback to the backup ingestion tool and mark the original job as retrying."
   - Expected: [call-primary -> detect-502 -> call-backup(with-preserved-args) -> job-state-update(retrying)]
   - Checks: preserve idempotency and avoid duplicate downstream notifications.

4) "Combine my last two expenses into one claim and split the total between project A and B by percent."
   - Expected: [user-history(fetch_last_n=2) -> expense-merge(ids) -> split-apply(percents:{A:60,B:40}) -> create-claim(payload)]
   - Ambiguity: percentages not provided -> should ask clarifying question rather than guessing.

5) "Generate a summary, then for each bullet that mentions 'security' create a ticket in jira with title = bullet_text."
   - Expected: [summarize(text) -> iterate(bullets) filter(keyword='security') -> jira-create(title=bullet_text, body=ctx)]
   - Failure mode: model returns todo list instead of iterating/calling jira.

Labeling & equivalence rules (important for evaluating pass/fail):
- Tool-selection: exact tool name match for critical actions; for fallback tools we allow any tool in the configured fallback list.
- Argument equivalence: numeric and date normalization allowed ("Oct 1" == "2024-10-01").
- Ordering tolerance: when operations are commutative (e.g., notify-bulk order), accept permutations.
- Clarification expectation: if user-provided info is clearly insufficient, expected behavior is to ask one clarifying question instead of guessing — mark as PASS if question issued.
- Idempotency: duplicated actions considered failure unless explicitly guarded by idempotency token.

Metrics definitions and thresholds:
- Tool-selection accuracy (top-1): fraction of cases where the first tool call equals canonical tool. Nightly threshold: >= 96%.
- Arg-parsing F1: macro F1 over argument slots (dates, ids, lists). Nightly threshold: >= 92%
- Chain-completion rate: fraction of cases that produce a complete valid sequence (all required calls made). Weekly threshold: >= 94%
- Clarification recall: fraction of ambiguous cases where model asked a clarifying question instead of guessing. Threshold: >= 90%
- Flakiness score: fraction of cases that change classification across 5 deterministic-seed runs. Target <= 2%.

Regression detection rules:
- Alert when any metric drops by >3 percentage points relative to baseline for the same model version.
- Hard fail if tool-selection accuracy <90% for any nightly run.
- Flag cases with increased flakiness (>+1.5%) for manual inspection.

Test harness and execution notes:
- Use deterministic sampling (temperature 0.0) for primary runs; record top-k logits to aid debugging.
- For tests meant to exercise nondeterminism (e.g., clarifying vs guessing), run with T=0.4 and measure variability across seeds.
- Ensure KV cache cleared between test cases where state leakage is not intended. Add explicit cache-reset call in harness where needed.
- Capture both structured function calls (preferred) and text fallbacks — label accordingly.

Labeling process and QA:
- Primary labels created by applied-ml engineers (2 reviewers per case).
- Ambiguous cases sent to product for final guidance on canonical behavior.
- Store labels in CSV with columns: case_id, prompt, canonical_sequence (pipe-separated), canonical_args (semi-colon separated), acceptance_notes.

Storage, naming convention, and test ids:
- Filenames: short kebab-case e.g., intake-merge-claim-003. Case ids: apl-cc-XXXX (apl for applied, cc = call-chaining).
- Store JSON fixtures under our eval S3 path and reference the S3 links in ingestion metadata.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we treat clarifying questions that move the user to a multi-turn planning flow as PASS? (proposal: yes, if single explicit question asked.)
- Define canonical fallback lists for overlapping tools (product input needed).
- Decide whether to include long-run performance / memory scenarios (KV growth) in this suite or separate it.

Next steps (owners):
- Samir: finalize canonical fallback lists (due 2024-11-08).
- Nora: implement harness changes to clear KV and record logits (PR: linked_artifacts item).
- Diego: curate the 30-case nightly quick-suite and labelers assignment (due 2024-11-15).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic and includes permissive equivalence rules to reduce false positives during onboarding. Please comment with any disagreements on canonical sequences for ambiguous cases.

Appendix: sample CSV label row example (one-line representation)
- "apl-cc-001","Find latest Q4 sales, extract >50k, notify","data-fetch|csv-parse|notify-bulk","query=Q4;filter=ARR>50000;template=prod-alert","accepts_numeric_commas=true"

End of document.
